messages:
Maya: quick one — support has a handful of escalations this morning where customers hit 429s shortly after deploy. not widespread but enough to worry. can we run a small, focused load sweep to pick sane defaults for RPM/TPM + burst windows?

Jae: can you paste an example 429 payload / headers from the customer? that'll help figure out whether it's quota exhaustion or our short-term burst caps.

Ellie: copying one from support ticket #12487: response body is generic rate_limit, headers included:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1670005123
Retry-After: 15
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "detail": "burst window exceeded" }
```

Customer says they saw a sudden spike (lambda warmup + retry storm) — calls peaked ~350 RPS for ~8s then dropped. they do streaming chat requests so token TPM matters too.

Tom: thanks. sounds like short, high-burst traffic pushed them over the token-bucket instant capacity. we should run two tests: one focusing on RPM/requests-level rate limiting (stateless frontdoor) and one on TPM/token-level (billing/usage-level) since TPM counting varies by model/tokens-per-request.

Priya: agree. propose test matrix:
- baseline steady-state: 5m at target RPS (50, 100, 300 rps) to validate sustained throughput and 95/99 p99 latencies
- burst window sweep: ramp 5s -> hold 10s -> drop, for burst sizes 2x, 4x, 8x nominal RPS
- token payload variation: small (100 tokens), medium (800 tokens), large (4k tokens) to catch TPM boundaries
- warmup/no-warmup: with connection pool warm vs cold start

Jae: good. what tooling? k6 or vegeta? I'd prefer k6 for realistic ramp stages and better percentile reporting. vegeta is good for high rate short bursts though.

Tom: let's do both. vegeta for very short, high-rps bursts (simulate retry storms), k6 for longer steady-state and ramping. example vegeta command for a short spike:

```
echo "POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer $KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ \"model\": \"rw-large\", \"input\": \"hello\" }" | 
  vegeta attack -duration=20s -rate=1000 -connections=400 | vegeta report
```

Priya: and k6 snippet for staged ramp + sustained:

```
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export let options = {
  stages: [
    { duration: '30s', target: 50 },
    { duration: '30s', target: 300 },
    { duration: '5m', target: 300 },
  ],
  thresholds: { 'http_req_duration{p99:yes}': ['p(99)<1000'] }
};
export default function () {
  http.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({ model: 'rw-medium', input: 'hello' }), { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + __ENV.KEY } });
  sleep(1);
}
```

Ellie: FYI support will provide a sample customer traffic trace (anonymized) — it has short bursts with backoff retries. might be useful to replay exact pattern.

Maya: good call. also let's capture the following metrics during runs:
- 429 count + origin (frontdoor vs quota service)
- X-RateLimit-* header values emitted by frontdoor
- backend queue depth / pending requests per instance
- cold-start counts and token-cache hit rates
- p50/p95/p99 latencies per model
- billing tokens consumed per minute (TPM)

Tom: will add CPU/GPU utilization, connection saturation, and kernel backpressure counters from runtime. also track KV cache eviction events — prefix cache warmup matters for chat workloads.

Jae: one more consideration: our burst policy is a two-level system — a short term burst allowance (burst_window_seconds, instant_bucket_tokens) and a longer-term rate window. for defaults we need to pick both, e.g. allow 2x instant burst for 10s, but enforce sustained rate afterward.

Priya: preliminary guesses (subject to validation):
- default per-key RPM: 360 requests/min (6 RPS sustained)
- default per-key TPM: 50k tokens/min
- burst multiplier: 3x for burst_window_seconds: 15s, with token-bucket refill configured to recover over 60s

Jae: those numbers feel high for new free-tier keys. we should have tiered defaults: free/dev, paid, enterprise. e.g.:
- free/dev: 60 RPM, 10k TPM, burst 2x/10s
- paid: 360 RPM, 50k TPM, burst 3x/15s
- enterprise: configurable / higher defaults + dedicated capacity

Maya: support-driven constraint: we want defaults that minimize transient escalations but don't open vector for abuse. so soft limits + clear Retry-After and dynamic backoff recommendations in docs.

Tom: action plan:
1) Priya/Tom run vegeta short-burst matrix (2m window with spikes at 1s, 5s, 10s) by EOD tomorrow.
2) Jae/Priya run k6 sustained/ramp profiles across token sizes, capture TPM effects, next day.
3) We'll reinspect emitted X-RateLimit headers and ensure they reflect remaining and reset correctly for both RPM and TPM.
4) follow-up meeting Fri 11am to pick defaults and update the rate-limit config repo.

Priya: starting vegeta runs now against staging. tagging loadbot to summarize results when done.

loadbot: running attack fleet — 6 pods will execute test matrix: burst-2x, burst-4x, burst-8x. ETA 14m. logging to /var/log/loadtests/1998001234/*.tar.gz

Ellie: thanks team. I'll relay that support will pause customer escalations mention in ticket until we have runs.

Maya: perfect. if we see 429s originating from the quota service (not frontdoor) we need to revisit TPM counting logic — last change to token accounting was two releases ago.

Jae: noted. I'll instrument a debug build that emits token-count per request to tracing so we can correlate token spikes to 429s.

Tom: also make sure to include a warmup run to estimate A ephemeral pool warmup latency; sometimes the first few seconds hit timeouts and trigger retries which amplify bursts.

Priya: first vegeta run finished: quick summary posted to the loadtest dashboard:
- spike 4x nominal (nominal=300rps) for 10s -> frontdoor issued 429s at ~7-9s mark.
- backend CPU stayed <70% but connection queue grew -> connection saturation + prefork limits.
- X-RateLimit-Limit emitted matched configured RPM but token bucket was drained faster for large-token requests.
Full logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/loadtests/1998001234/report.html (internal)

Maya: great, leave results in the ticket. we'll reconvene after k6 runs and pick tier defaults. please note any surprising replay patterns. (reaction :eyes:)
